body.statement: Uniformly over \(\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}(\alpha,\beta,L,c,\varepsilon)\), the deterministic lower-envelope quotas and the interval \(I_{T,\Delta}\) remain uniformly honest and have expected length at most a constant multiple of \(r_{T,\Delta}\). This is the achievability reduction under the one-sided polynomial forced-exploration condition used by Shi, Wang, and Wu. No matching \(T^{-(1-\alpha)/2}\) converse is asserted on this enlarged class because policies may allocate the designated arm more often than order \(t^{-\alpha}\).
body.justification: This separates the one-sided condition needed for a policy-uniform upper bound from the two-sided comparability regime needed to identify an exact minimax sampling frontier.
body.gap: Shi, Wang, and Wu use one-sided forced exploration for delayed asymptotic inference under outcome-delay independence; the proposition isolates what survives under unrestricted outcome-delay dependence without attributing the new two-sided regime to them.
body.consumer: Analysts whose logs certify only a forced-exploration floor can retain the honest construction while reporting an upper guarantee rather than an exact policy-class minimax rate.
body.proof_tex:
The proof of lem:quota-success uses only ass:one-sided-forced-exploration for arm \(1\) and ass:control-floor for arm \(0\); therefore its deterministic quota guarantee holds uniformly on \(\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}\).  Lem:arm-tape-equivalence and lem:old-cohort-correction also hold on that class.  The concentration, gate, and studentization arguments in thm:uniform-gated-inference use the policy only through those deterministic quotas.  They therefore give
\[
 \inf_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}}
 P\{\tau\in I_{T,\Delta}\}\geq1-\eta-o(1).
\]
The branchwise length calculation in the proof of thm:minimax-length-frontier likewise uses only the quota orders and the delay envelope, and hence gives
\[
 \sup_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}}
 E_{P,\Pi}|I_{T,\Delta}|\leq C_\eta r_{T,\Delta}.
\]
The lower allocation envelope alone does not bound the actual number of designated-arm assignments from above.  Thus it cannot yield the sampling-information obstruction used in the converse, which is why no matching sampling lower bound is concluded on this enlarged class.
